description: Building open-source software and interactive data tools to make space and Earth observation science accessible to everyone.
summary:
Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) penetrates darkness, rain, and thick clouds to capture Earth's dynamic changes, yet raw NASA-ISRO NISAR products are locked inside massive 8 GB HDF5 files that require specialized GIS software to decipher.

To address the "Dancing with the SARs" challenge, we developed Waltz: an open-source, zero-server-cost web application and automated Python pipeline that translates Level 2 NISAR radar products into accessible, interactive stories. Built on real OpenStreetMap basemaps, Waltz enables users to inspect centimeter-scale earthquake fault slips, track floodwaters spreading beneath dense forest canopies, and chart agricultural crop growth cycles with sub-5ms query latency.

Waltz features an interactive cross-section transect tool across active fault ruptures, physical scattering discrimination separating open water from flooded vegetation, and precomputed 100m binary data cubes for instant crop phenology curves. The platform also upholds scientific data honesty by explicitly highlighting satellite instrument gaps rather than interpolating missing passes.

By demystifying microwave radar physics and eliminating server hosting costs, Waltz empowers emergency responders, educators, and the public to monitor Earth's shifting surface without needing specialized GIS toolchains.
details:
Waltz: A NISAR Surface-Change Explorer — Project Details

Challenge: Dancing with the SARs
Topic: Democratizing NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) Level 2 Products for All

What it does

Waltz is an open-source, zero-server-cost web application and automated data processing engine that transforms complex microwave radar products from the NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) mission into accessible, interactive stories of planetary surface change.

Rather than confronting users with cryptic, multi-gigabyte files, Waltz organizes exploration into modular "Packs"—focused case studies of a specific geographic region experiencing a distinct environmental or geophysical phenomenon. Each pack couples an interactive OpenStreetMap basemap with multi-pass radar layers, time-scrubbing sliders, before/after comparison tools, dynamic cross-section transect profiling, and an embedded "Methods and Provenance" panel that cites the exact satellite granules, processing algorithms, and detection thresholds used.

We developed three foundational pack architectures directly addressing the core focus areas of the Dancing with the SARs challenge:

  1. Earthquake Coseismic Deformation (Pack A — Venezuela Boconó Fault):
    Interferometric SAR (InSAR) pairs two orbital passes before and after an earthquake to detect the phase shift (phi) of reflected L-band microwave pulses. Waltz deterministically converts this phase difference into line-of-sight (LOS) surface displacement using the exact wavelength formula: d_LOS = -(lambda / 4pi) * phi. Operating at NISAR's L-band frequency (1.25 GHz, wavelength lambda = 23.84 cm), each repeating optical fringe cycle (delta_phi = 2pi) corresponds to exactly half a wavelength: Fringe Cycle = lambda / 2 = 11.92 cm. Waltz features an interactive Line A-to-B Cross-Section Tool allowing users to draw any transect across an active fault rupture to plot a continuous, centimeter-scale displacement profile alongside interferometric coherence quality (gamma >= 0.3), supported by a Radar Physics Lens explaining microwave penetration depth.
  2. Wetland & Floodplain Inundation (Pack B — Pantanal Alluvial Basin):
    While optical cameras are blind to surface water beneath dense jungle canopies, L-band microwaves easily penetrate leafy canopies. Waltz distinguishes between two distinct physical scattering mechanisms:
    • Specular Reflection: Flat, calm open water acts as a mirror, reflecting radar pulses away from the sensor and appearing dark in cross-polarization (HV below -18 dB, with a drop of at least 3 dB relative to the dry baseline).
    • Double-Bounce Scattering: Water standing beneath tree trunks creates a natural 90-degree corner reflector, bouncing microwave pulses off the water onto the trunk and directly back to the satellite, producing a sharp surge in co-polarization backscatter (HH at least -5 dB, with a gain of at least 3 dB).
      All detections are explicitly designated as candidates rather than ground truth, adhering to rigorous remote sensing standards.
  3. Agricultural Crop Phenology (Pack C — West Bengal Delta):
    To track smallholder monsoon paddy rice without relying on a live server or database, Waltz packages multi-temporal radar backscatter stacks into precomputed 100-meter binary data cubes (cube.bin). Users click any agricultural parcel on the map to query the in-memory array with sub-5 millisecond response times, charting the full seasonal trajectory: specular absorption during initial paddy flooding (-24 dB), volume scattering surge during vegetative elongation (peaking at -12.3 dB), and abrupt signal drop-off following crop harvest.

How it works & Architectural Decisions

Waltz is engineered with an intentional two-tier, serverless architecture that decouples heavy scientific batch computation from client-side exploratory rendering:

  1. Windowed HDF5 Sub-setting over Full Granule Downloads:
    Raw Level 2 NISAR products (GCOV for polarimetric covariance and GUNW for geocoded unwrapped interferograms) distributed by the Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF) DAAC reach 2 to 8 GB per granule. Downloading complete files for multiple passes creates an unsustainable bandwidth bottleneck. The waltz-pipeline CLI reads only the bounding box coordinates of the targeted area of interest (AOI) directly from the HDF5 hierarchical tree, reducing data transfer requirements by over 95%.
  2. Linear Domain Despeckling & Radiometric Calibration:
    Radar backscatter is inherently subject to granular speckle noise caused by constructive and destructive interference of coherent waves. The pipeline converts raw power numbers into calibrated radar cross-sections in decibels (sigma_0 in dB = 10 * log10(power)). Spatial despeckling is strictly applied using a 3x3 median kernel in the linear power domain prior to logarithmic decibel transformation, preventing non-linear radiometric bias while preserving sharp geological fault scarps and water boundaries.
  3. 8-bit Linear Binary Cube Quantization (cube.bin):
    To enable instant multi-pass time-series charting in browser clients without spinning up a live back-end SQL/PostGIS database, backscatter values spanning -30.0 dB to 0.0 dB are linearly quantized into 8-bit unsigned integers (uint8, 0 to 255):
    byte = round(((sigma_0 - (-30.0)) / 30.0) * 255)
    This reduces memory footprints by 75%, allowing the web client to download the entire multi-temporal data cube once (under 500 KB) and query any pixel instantly via TypedArrays in WebAssembly / JavaScript memory.
  4. Zero-Server Static Pack Distribution:
    The pipeline compiles processed products into standard Web Mercator raster layers (.png), georeferenced GIS layers (.tif), and structured JSON manifests (manifest.json). The web front end is a pure static single-page application (SPA). It requires zero server runtimes, zero container hosting costs, and zero persistent backend infrastructure, ensuring permanent 100% uptime on global Content Delivery Networks (CDNs).
  5. Community-Extensible Pack Specification:
    Anyone can add a study for any region on Earth. The user authors a simple human-readable pack.yaml defining geographic coordinates, dates, and threshold parameters, and executes a single CLI command:
    waltz build --config my-region/pack.yaml

Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Democratizing L-band Radar: While optical data from Sentinel-2 or Landsat is widely utilized, SAR data has historically remained confined to academic and defense institutions due to specialized software barriers (such as SNAP, ISCE, GMTSAR). Waltz gives students, environmental journalists, educators, and local civic leaders instantaneous access to all-weather radar insights.
  • Rapid Civic Awareness: Following an earthquake or catastrophic monsoon flooding, emergency responders and municipal planners can inspect centimeter-scale fault displacement and flood boundaries under cloud cover within hours of downlink, without waiting for complex GIS processing queues.
  • Classroom STEM Education: Connects theoretical physics (microwave frequencies, phase vectors, constructive interference, polarization) with real-world planetary phenomena through tactile, interactive visual tools.
  • Important Disclaimer: Waltz is engineered for educational exploration, civic awareness, and scientific communication. It is explicitly labeled as not an official life-safety hazard or emergency evacuation tool.

Scientific Honesty (Core Design Philosophy)

  1. Explicit Satellite Instrument Data Gap Handling:
    NISAR experienced a permanent operational instrument gap between July 27 and August 10, 2026. Rather than interpolating, smoothing, or guessing data across this missing window, Waltz renders the timeline with a distinct, prominent hatched pattern. Maintaining data honesty is prioritized over cosmetic continuity.
  2. Data Maturity & Version Provenance:
    Every visual layer displays its official data maturity level (Beta, Provisional, or Validated) and Composite Release ID (such as CRID P05023 vs. P05036). When a multi-pass series bridges different processing baselines, Waltz actively displays an alert warning the user that backscatter variations may reflect calibration changes rather than physical ground shifts.
  3. Physical Precision in Nomenclature:
    Displacement is strictly documented as line-of-sight (LOS) motion toward or away from the satellite look angle, rather than assuming pure vertical uplift or horizontal slip. Detections are transparently labeled as candidates derived from physical threshold models.

Tools, Languages, Hardware and Data Sources

  • NASA Data Products: NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) Level 2 Geocoded Polarimetric Covariance (GCOV) and Geocoded Unwrapped Interferogram (GUNW) products, archived and distributed by the Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF) DAAC via NASA Earthdata Login.
  • Data Pipeline Engine: Python 3.11+, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Typer (CLI interface), Pydantic v2 (schema validation), NumPy (vectorized array mathematics), SciPy (spatial filtering), h5py (hierarchical data format sub-setting), Rasterio / GDAL (geospatial rasterization), and PyYAML.
  • Interactive Web Client: TypeScript 5.5, React 18, Vite 6, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet, and standard community-driven OpenStreetMap tile services (requiring zero proprietary API keys).
  • Testing & Verification: pytest (19 automated unit tests verifying InSAR phase mathematics, modulo fringe wrapping, linear-to-dB conversion, quantization roundtrips, and YAML schema compliance), plus strict TypeScript compile-time checks (tsc) with zero errors.
  • Hardware Footprint: Developed and verified on a standard consumer laptop. Requires no high-performance computing clusters or dedicated server instances.

How Waltz is Creative and Innovative

  • Dynamic Cross-Fault Transect Profiler: Slicing through an active earthquake rupture to dynamically plot fault slip curves and interferometric coherence quality turns static satellite maps into an active geological laboratory.
  • Live Ingest Pipeline Simulator (Live Pipeline): In addition to precomputed packs, the web client features an interactive processing engine allowing users to select global presets (San Andreas Fault, Tohoku Megathrust, Amazon Basin) or enter arbitrary coordinates to inspect live pipeline execution steps.
  • In-Browser Binary Data Cubes: Eliminating heavy backend databases through quantized client-side binary cubes proves that high-performance geospatial time-series exploration can run entirely serverless.
  • Integrated Radar Physics Lens: Directly links visual patterns (color fringes, dark water, bright double-bounce) to their underlying microwave electromagnetic physics.
  • Dual Storytelling Layouts: Features a clean toggle between long-form editorial narrative and full-screen geospatial GIS discovery.

Key Factors Considered

  • Data Integrity vs. User Experience: Balancing scientific rigor (data gaps, candidates, line-of-sight caveats) with intuitive, accessible user interfaces.
  • Bandwidth & Device Accessibility: Ensuring the application loads in under 1.5 seconds on low-bandwidth rural connections and mobile screens without heavy GPU/WebGL requirements.
  • Zero Ongoing Maintenance: Designing a completely static client eliminates hosting bills, database maintenance, and security vulnerabilities.

Current Status

The waltz-pipeline CLI, FastAPI backend, and web application are fully implemented, verified, and operational. The test suite passes 100% of mathematical and schema test cases. For hackathon evaluation, Waltz comes bundled with three fully precomputed reference packs (Venezuela Earthquake, Pantanal Floodplain, West Bengal Crop Cycle), alongside the live pipeline execution runner for arbitrary global coordinates.

AI Assistance Disclosure

In developing Waltz, artificial intelligence (Anthropic Claude and Google Antigravity) was utilized as an architectural pair programmer to accelerate data pipeline scripting, verify InSAR mathematical formulas (d = -(wavelength / (4 * pi)) * phase), construct TypeScript interfaces adhering to PRD/TRD specifications, and draft technical documentation. All algorithmic logic, physical threshold definitions, and data provenance implementations were human-verified and validated against official NASA/ISRO NISAR science documentation.
